0.long_answer: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a neuromuscular disorder that causes progressive muscle wasting due to degeneration of motor neurons in the anterior horn of the spinal cord. It is the most common genetic cause of infant death when left untreated. This condition is generally caused by a mutation in the SMN1 gene located on chromosome 5q13. The SMN1 gene is essential for the production of the survival motor neuron (SMN) protein, which is crucial for maintaining the health and function of motor neurons. A mutation in this gene leads to reduced levels of functional SMN protein, resulting in the degeneration of motor neurons and subsequent muscular atrophy.
